screen: Audit Log List (SCR-ADM-05) and Audit Log Details (SCR-ADM-05-D1)
preconditions: The Admin is logged in to BPMS.
The Admin's role has the "audit_log:view" permission with scope All.
Audit records exist, written automatically whenever business data is created, updated, deleted or soft-deleted.

process.title: Access Audit Log Screen
process.detail: The Admin opens System administration > Audit log, or follows an "View audit log" link from another screen, which pre-fills the entity, entity ID, actor, action and date filters.

process.title: Load Audit Log List
process.detail: The system sends a request to GET /audit-logs with page 1, page size 20, the current filters and the sort order "Newest first".

process.title: Retrieve Audit Records
process.detail: The server retrieves matching audit records from the database, including time, actor, action, entity name, entity ID, IP address and changed columns, together with the total record count.

process.title: Display Audit Log Table
process.detail: The system displays the records in a table with the columns Time, Actor, Action, Entity, Entity ID, IP address and Changed columns, and shows the total number of records and the current page (e.g. "Page 1/5"). Changes made by background jobs show "System" as the actor.

process.title: Filter and Sort Records
process.detail: The Admin can search by entity, ID or actor, enter an entity name, choose an action (Create, Update, Delete, Soft delete), choose a From date and To date, and select "Newest first" or "Oldest first", then click "Apply". "Clear filters" resets all filters and reloads the list from page 1.

process.title: Navigate Pages
process.detail: The Admin clicks "Previous page" or "Next page" to move between pages of 20 records.

process.title: View Audit Log Details
process.detail: The Admin clicks a row or "View details". The system sends a request to GET /audit-logs/{id} and opens the details drawer with three sections: General (time, actor, account ID, entity, entity ID, action), HTTP request (IP address, method, path, browser/client, trace ID) and Data changes (column, old value, new value).

process.title: Close Details
process.detail: The Admin clicks the close button or presses Esc to close the drawer and return to the list.

postconditions: The Admin views the audit records that match the selected filters, sorted and paged as requested.
If the Admin opens a record, the system displays its full details, including the old and new values of each changed column.
No audit record is created, changed or deleted by this screen; it is read-only.

errors.title: No Matching Records
errors.detail: Display the message "No matching audit records." in the table.

errors.title: Invalid Date Range
errors.detail: When the From date is after the To date, display "The start date must be on or before the end date." and disable the "Apply" button.

errors.title: Audit Log Could Not Be Loaded
errors.detail: Display "Could not load the audit log." with a "Retry" button that reloads the list.

errors.title: Record No Longer Exists
errors.detail: When the details request returns 404, display "This audit record no longer exists." in the drawer.

errors.title: Details Could Not Be Loaded
errors.detail: Display "Could not load the audit log details." in the drawer.

errors.title: Unauthorized or Forbidden Access
errors.detail: If the session has expired (401) the user is redirected to sign in; if the user lacks the "audit_log:view" permission (403) the request is rejected.

security: Both endpoints require authentication and the "audit_log:view" permission with scope All, enforced on the server.
The audit log is read-only: no API exists to edit or delete audit records.
Sensitive values such as passwords, tokens and secrets are masked as "***" in old and new values.
Filtering, paging and sorting are performed on the server, and page size is limited so the client cannot request unbounded data.
